root:
Puerto — Rust full-stack DDD framework

Usage: puerto <COMMAND>

Commands:
  new          Scaffold a new Puerto project
  generate     Code generators for existing Puerto projects
  list         List entities and use cases defined in puerto.toml
  validate     Validate puerto.toml (field types, names, entity consistency)
  completions  Print shell completion script
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version
generate:
Code generators for existing Puerto projects

Usage: puerto generate <COMMAND>

Commands:
  scaffold      Scaffold all DDD layers for a new entity (db and CRUD inferred from puerto.toml)
  use-case      Add a use case to an existing entity
  event         Declare a custom domain event of a CRUD entity and regenerate its events.rs
                (projects created with --events)
  consumer      Add a consumer to the worker: an event handler, its tests and its registry entry
                (projects created with --events)
  mail          Add a mail: its port, its template implementation and its templates (subject.txt,
                body.html, body.txt). The first one also adds Mailpit and SMTP_URL / MAIL_FROM to
                .env
  bootstrap     Regenerate presentation/src/generated/bootstrap.rs from puerto.toml
  migration     Create a new SQLx migration file
  snippets      Write IDE snippet files (.zed/snippets/rust.json, .vscode/puerto.code-snippets)
  domain        Scaffold only the domain layer for a new entity (domain-first workflow)
  application   Scaffold only the application layer for an existing entity
  repository    Scaffold only the repository (infrastructure) layer for an existing entity
  presentation  Scaffold only the presentation layer for an existing entity (regenerates
                bootstrap.rs)
  web           Scaffold only the frontend slice of an existing CRUD entity (web projects;
                regenerates web/src/presentation/core/generated/)
  value-object  Declare a shared value object in puerto.toml (reusable across entities)
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

commands.help:
Scaffold a new Puerto project

Usage: puerto new [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --name <NAME>                Project name (skips interactive prompt)
      --db                         Include database support (SQLx + Postgres) (skips interactive
                                   prompt)
      --no-db                      Explicitly skip database support without prompting
      --no-demo                    Skip the Greeting demo entity (creates an empty project)
      --no-web                     Skip the web frontend (`web/`: React + daisyUI on Bun)
      --events <EVENTS>            Domain events (needs --db): every write records an event in an
                                   outbox, relayed through this transport [possible values: db,
                                   kafka]
      --auth <AUTH>                Auth: `oidc` verifies an OpenID Connect provider's tokens (Auth0,
                                   Keycloak — Keycloak runs in docker-compose.yml for development);
                                   `local` keeps accounts and sessions in the project's database
                                   (needs --db) [possible values: oidc, local]
      --destination <DESTINATION>  Directory where the project will be created (defaults to current
                                   directory)
  -h, --help                       Print help

Scaffold all DDD layers for a new entity (db and CRUD inferred from puerto.toml)

Usage: puerto generate scaffold [OPTIONS] <NAME> [-- <FIELDS>...]

Arguments:
  <NAME>       Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Product, OrderItem)
  [FIELDS]...  Fields after -- separator. Primitives: title:String price:i64! desc:opt:String
               tags:vec:String Value Objects: name:Name:String age:Age:i64
               status:Status:enum:Active/Inactive mid:Mid:opt:String Shared VO (type inferred from
               puerto.toml): email:Email

Options:
      --force            Overwrite an already-generated entity, discarding hand-written changes in
                         its files
      --public <PUBLIC>  Auth projects: use cases whose routes need no token, comma-separated (e.g.
                         list_products,get_product). Every other route takes `auth: BearerAuth`
      --role <ROLE>      Auth projects: a role a route requires, <use_case>=<role>, comma-separated
                         (e.g. create_product=admin,delete_product=admin) — `#[require_role]` on the
                         handler
  -h, --help             Print help

Add a use case to an existing entity

Usage: puerto generate use-case <ENTITY> <ACTION>

Arguments:
  <ENTITY>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Product)
  <ACTION>  Use case action in snake_case (e.g. delete_product)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Declare a shared value object in puerto.toml (reusable across entities)

Usage: puerto generate value-object <NAME> <INNER_TYPE>

Arguments:
  <NAME>        Value object name in PascalCase (e.g. Email, Money)
  <INNER_TYPE>  Inner primitive type: String, i64, bool, f64, Uuid, DateTime

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Create a new SQLx migration file

Usage: puerto generate migration <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Migration name in snake_case (e.g. add_products_table)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Declare a custom domain event of a CRUD entity and regenerate its events.rs (projects created with
--events)

Usage: puerto generate event <ENTITY> <NAME>

Arguments:
  <ENTITY>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Product)
  <NAME>    Event type in snake_case, past tense (e.g. product_published)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Add a consumer to the worker: an event handler, its tests and its registry entry (projects created
with --events)

Usage: puerto generate consumer --on <ON> <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Consumer name in snake_case (e.g. notify_new_product)

Options:
      --on <ON>  The event types it handles, comma-separated (e.g.
                 product_created,product_published)
  -h, --help     Print help

Add a mail: its port, its template implementation and its templates (subject.txt, body.html,
body.txt). The first one also adds Mailpit and SMTP_URL / MAIL_FROM to .env

Usage: puerto generate mail [OPTIONS] <NAME> [-- <FIELDS>...]

Arguments:
  <NAME>       Mail name in snake_case (e.g. welcome, order_shipped)
  [FIELDS]...  The values its text shows, after --: name:String seats:i64 plan:opt:String.
               Primitives and opt:<type> only; the recipient `to` is always there. None: name:String

Options:
      --on <ON>  Projects created with --events: the worker sends the mail on these event types,
                 comma-separated (e.g. customer_created). Its fields come from the events' snapshots
      --to <TO>  With --on: the String field of the snapshot that holds the recipient (e.g. email)
  -h, --help     Print help

Scaffold only the frontend slice of an existing CRUD entity (web projects; regenerates
web/src/presentation/core/generated/)

Usage: puerto generate web [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Product)

Options:
      --force  Overwrite the entity's existing frontend files, discarding hand-written changes
  -h, --help   Print help

Scaffold only the domain layer for a new entity (domain-first workflow)

Usage: puerto generate domain <NAME> [-- <FIELDS>...]

Arguments:
  <NAME>       Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Product, OrderItem)
  [FIELDS]...  Fields after -- separator. Same syntax as `generate scaffold`. They are written to
               puerto.toml, so `generate application/repository/presentation` pick them up

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Scaffold only the application layer for an existing entity

Usage: puerto generate application <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Product)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Scaffold only the repository (infrastructure) layer for an existing entity

Usage: puerto generate repository <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Product)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Scaffold only the presentation layer for an existing entity (regenerates bootstrap.rs)

Usage: puerto generate presentation <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Entity name in PascalCase (e.g. Product)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Regenerate presentation/src/generated/bootstrap.rs from puerto.toml

Usage: puerto generate bootstrap [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --allow-missing  Write the file even when puerto.toml declares entities whose code is not on
                       disk
  -h, --help           Print help

Write IDE snippet files (.zed/snippets/rust.json, .vscode/puerto.code-snippets)

Usage: puerto generate snippets [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --ide <IDE>  Target IDE: zed or vscode (default: both)
  -h, --help       Print help

List entities and use cases defined in puerto.toml

Usage: puerto list

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Validate puerto.toml (field types, names, entity consistency)

Usage: puerto validate

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Print shell completion script

Usage: puerto completions <SHELL>

Arguments:
  <SHELL>  Shell to generate completions for (bash, zsh, fish, powershell) [possible values: bash,
           elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
